solutions.check: grid and clues read from the FT's printable PDF, its numbering matching the clue list; every fifteensquared answer written into it with each crossing agreeing

clue.text: Pole visiting a Scottish island

indicators.note: the pole is calling on the letter, so the two pieces stand side by side

parts.note: a pole is a staff, a long stick

explanation.surface: Someone from Poland pays a trip to an island off Scotland.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Pole' looks like a Polish person; it is a stick. STAFFA is a small island in the Inner Hebrides, home of Fingal's Cave.
explanation.definitionFit: Staffa is an uninhabited island of the Inner Hebrides, off the west coast of Scotland.

clue.text: Couple of strikes, disorganised

parts.note: to slap is to strike with the open hand
to dash is to strike or hurl violently

explanation.surface: Two hits in quick succession leave a boxer in disarray.
explanation.definitionFit: Something slapdash is done hastily and carelessly, hence disorganised.

clue.text: Change involving centigrade causes an argument

indicators.note: involving means the change takes in the temperature letter within itself

parts.note: an alteration is a change
C is the abbreviation for centigrade

explanation.surface: Altering the thermostat to Celsius starts a domestic row.
explanation.definitionFit: An altercation is a noisy quarrel, a heated argument.

clue.text: Female with superb features

parts.note: ace is slang for excellent or superb

explanation.surface: A woman is praised for her beautiful looks.
explanation.walkthrough: 'features' is a plural noun in the surface; as the definition, face and features both mean the countenance.
explanation.definitionFit: One's features collectively make up the face, the look of a person's countenance.

clue.text: Vehicle in street ahead of a crock, reconditioned

indicators.note: in an across answer, ahead of puts the street abbreviation first
reconditioned means the letters of 'a crock' are reworked into a new order

explanation.surface: An old banger in the road has been done up.
explanation.walkthrough: 'reconditioned' looks like a description of the old car; it rearranges A CROCK into OCKCAR. 'crock' is British slang for a decrepit old vehicle.
explanation.definitionFit: A stock car is a car modified for racing on oval tracks, a kind of vehicle.

clue.text: Poet in New York entering verse-making contest

indicators.note: entering means the city abbreviation goes inside the contest word

parts.note: a tenson was a contest in verse between troubadours

explanation.surface: A poet from New York signs up for a poetry competition.
explanation.walkthrough: TENSON is an obscure word for a troubadours' poetic debate.
explanation.definitionFit: Alfred, Lord Tennyson was the Victorian Poet Laureate, a famous English poet.

clue.text: Marketable plug

definitions.meaning: a ... product is one fit for sale on the market
a plug is a broadcast advertisement, a television or radio spot

explanation.definitionFit: Commercial means saleable for profit; as a noun it is a broadcast advert, informally a plug.

clue.text: Working after drop of cognac in study

indicators.note: after means the working word follows the letter from the brandy
a drop of a drink is a little of it, here just its first letter

parts.note: on means working, as a machine that is on

explanation.surface: Someone works better after a nip of brandy while studying.
explanation.definitionFit: To con is an old verb meaning to study or learn by heart.

clue.text: Savour some sorrel? I shall

indicators.note: some says the answer is a run of letters hidden inside the words that follow

parts.note: the letters run across the end of one word into the next

explanation.surface: Someone wonders whether to try a little of the herb sorrel.
explanation.definitionFit: To relish food is to enjoy its taste, to savour it.

clue.text: Teacher has broken a Patsy Cline record

indicators.note: broken means the letters of 'Teacher has' are smashed and reassembled

explanation.surface: A schoolteacher has smashed a vinyl disc of a country singer.
explanation.walkthrough: 'has' looks like a link verb but its letters are fodder; 'broken' rearranges TEACHER HAS. Patsy Cline was an American country singer of the early 1960s.
explanation.definitionFit: Heartaches was a 1962 single recorded by country star Patsy Cline.

clue.text: Piece in paper, tiny piece with no heading

indicators.note: with no heading means the word loses its first letter, its head

parts.note: a particle is a tiny piece of matter

explanation.surface: A newspaper item turns out to be a small fragment missing its headline.
explanation.definitionFit: An article is a written piece in a newspaper or magazine.

clue.text: Lion man trained for virtually nothing

indicators.note: trained means the letters are drilled into a new formation

explanation.surface: A lion tamer works for hardly any pay.
explanation.definitionFit: A nominal fee or rent is a token amount, so small it is practically free.

clue.text: Small daughter on craft brings out tuck

parts.note: lower-case d, small, is the abbreviation for daughter
art is skill or craft

explanation.surface: A little girl at needlework learns to sew a fold.
explanation.definitionFit: In dressmaking a dart is a stitched tapering fold, a tuck to shape a garment.

clue.text: Fight corrupt sailor in South American port

parts.note: a fray is a brawl or fight
bent is slang for corrupt or dishonest
OS stands for ordinary seaman, a sailor

explanation.surface: A dodgy seaman gets into a brawl at a harbour in South America.
explanation.definitionFit: Fray Bentos is a river port in Uruguay, famous for its meat-packing industry.

clue.text: Vocalist on the Light Programme?

parts.note: the Light Programme was an old BBC radio station; read literally, a vocalist on a light is one who sings of a flame or lamp

explanation.definitionFit: A torch singer performs sentimental ballads of unrequited love, a sort of vocalist.

clue.text: Ready to start the day at university, an expert abroad

parts.note: up means in residence at university, as in up at Oxford
a dab, or dab hand, is an expert
abroad means out and about, outside

explanation.surface: A student expert from overseas is ready for the morning.
explanation.definitionFit: To be up and about is to be out of bed and active, set for the day.

clue.text: Seafood, bit of shellfish, affected one

indicators.note: a bit of the word here is only its opening letter

parts.note: camp means affected or exaggerated in manner
I is the Roman numeral for one

explanation.surface: A diner fussily picks at a morsel of shellfish.
explanation.definitionFit: Scampi are langoustine tails, usually fried in breadcrumbs, a seafood dish.

clue.text: Toscanini crept off to find Vladimir Horowitz, perhaps

indicators.note: off means the letters have gone bad, so they are out of order

explanation.surface: The conductor Toscanini slipped away to meet the great pianist Horowitz.
explanation.walkthrough: 'off' rearranges TOSCANINI CREPT. Vladimir Horowitz was a Russian-American virtuoso; 'perhaps' marks him as an example.
explanation.definitionFit: Horowitz was a renowned performer of piano recitals and concertos, an example of the classical virtuoso.

clue.text: In addition, a bigwig meets a head of state

parts.note: a swell is a fashionable or important person, a bigwig

indicators.note: head of means the opening letter of the following word

explanation.surface: A grandee greets a visiting president.
explanation.definitionFit: As well as means besides or in addition to.

clue.text: Fashionable suit, to a great extent

parts.note: in means fashionable
spades is one of the four suits in a pack of cards

explanation.surface: A trendy outfit is worn in abundance.
explanation.definitionFit: In spades is an idiom meaning in large amounts or to a high degree.

clue.text: See 17
10 describing pain in a German spa

indicators.note: describing means drawing round, so the article encloses the pain

parts.note: 10 across is ARTICLE, and AN is an indefinite article
an ache is a pain

explanation.surface: An article about aches at a health resort in Germany.
explanation.walkthrough: 'describing' is used in its geometric sense of drawing a line round.
explanation.definitionFit: Aachen, in western Germany, is an ancient spa town famed for hot springs.

clue.text: Son was worried, and frightened

parts.note: cared means was concerned or worried

explanation.surface: A boy was anxious and afraid.
explanation.definitionFit: Scared means afraid or frightened.

clue.text: See 9
Calves, once treated, recover from illness

indicators.note: treated means the letters are processed into a new arrangement

explanation.surface: Young cattle that were once given medicine get better.
explanation.definitionFit: To convalesce is to regain health gradually after being ill.

clue.text: Wet, head of wretched scallywag

indicators.note: head of picks out the first letter of the word after it

parts.note: an imp is a mischievous child, a scallywag

explanation.surface: A miserable rascal's leader is soaked.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Wet' looks like an adjective meaning damp; in British slang a wet is a feeble person.
explanation.definitionFit: Wet is British slang for a weak, ineffectual person, a weakling.

clue.text: Knowing tramp's lost hat

indicators.note: lost hat means the word loses its top letter, as in a down answer

parts.note: to march is to tramp, walk heavily; the 's reads as has

explanation.surface: A clever vagrant has mislaid his cap.
explanation.definitionFit: Arch means slyly knowing or mischievous, as in an arch look.

clue.text: Dog barking during brief meeting, seeing cat

indicators.note: during means the scrambled letters sit inside the shortened meeting
brief means the word is cut short by its last letter

parts.note: a rally is a mass meeting

indicators.note: barking is slang for mad, so the letters are scrambled

explanation.surface: A dog yaps through a short gathering when it spots a cat.
explanation.walkthrough: 'barking' is British slang for mad, so it scrambles the letters; the shortened meeting is RALL, which holds GDO. 'seeing' merely links the wordplay to the definition.
explanation.definitionFit: A Ragdoll is a breed of large, docile, blue-eyed cat.

clue.text: Doctor saving a space

indicators.note: saving means keeping, so the doctor holds the letter inside

parts.note: a GP is a general practitioner, a family doctor

explanation.surface: A physician keeps a place free.
explanation.walkthrough: GP, a general practitioner, is the British term for a family doctor.
explanation.definitionFit: A gap is an opening or empty space.

clue.text: Angered, terribly!

indicators.note: terribly signals that the letters of the word before it are thrown into disorder

explanation.surface: Someone is dreadfully cross.
explanation.walkthrough: The whole clue defines and is the wordplay: 'terribly' rearranges ANGERED, and terribly angered is the meaning.
explanation.definitionFit: Being enraged means being made furious, very angry indeed.

clue.text: Sub's place is in river?

indicators.note: in means the placing words sit inside the river

parts.note: the Dee is a river in Scotland, and another in Wales and England
to put is to place

explanation.surface: A submarine's location is somewhere in a river.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Sub' looks like a noun, a submarine; here it is a verb, to stand in for someone.
explanation.definitionFit: To sub for someone is to stand in, to deputise in their place.

clue.text: Section of song about mythological god

parts.note: C, for circa, means about
Horus is the falcon-headed god of Egyptian mythology

explanation.surface: Part of a song is devoted to an ancient deity.
explanation.definitionFit: The chorus is the refrain of a song, repeated after each verse.
